title: Scabbard: LLVM Instrumentation-aided Race Checking in CPU/GPU Unified Memory for AMD GPUs
problem: Data races in CPU/GPU unified memory systems go undetected; existing data-race checkers cannot detect races in heterogeneous systems using Unified Heterogeneous Memory (UHM)
motivation: AMD GPUs with Unified Heterogeneous Memory simplify programming by eliminating explicit data movement between CPU and GPU. However, this simplification introduces risk: data races across CPU-GPU boundaries are invisible to existing tools, threatening correctness.
method: LLVM pass-based instrumentation of both CPU and GPU code for unified memory systems; insertion of trace recording for writes, reads, and synchronizations; offline trace analysis to detect races; integration into AMD ROCm/HIP compilation toolchain
key_novelty: First tool to detect data races in CPU/GPU unified memory systems; novel LLVM implementation approach enabling cross-device race detection
contributions: Scabbard: First CPU/GPU unified memory race detector
LLVM pass plugin implementation for race instrumentation
Unified approach instrumenting both CPU and GPU code
Runtime trace recording of memory operations
Offline trace analysis for race detection
Documentation of LLVM implementation challenges for GPU/CPU tools
hardware_target: AMD GPUs with Unified Heterogeneous Memory (UHM)
baselines: Existing GPU race detectors (limited to GPU only)
limitations: Limited to AMD ROCm (generalization to CUDA/OpenCL unclear); overhead of offline trace analysis not detailed; scalability to large traces unclear
primary_theme: Race Detection for CPU-GPU Unified Memory
